text.headline: Bitcoin declines as exchange funds exit
text.tone: Confirmed outflows from major digital asset funds weighed on prices, even as broader market sentiment showed signs of recovery in other asset classes.
lead: Bitcoin fell 2.1% to $59,230 on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] page. Ether also retreated, losing 2.5%. This move coincided with a broader decline in digital asset market capitalization.

The decline is consistent with confirmed reports of capital flight, including a record exodus from a major Bitcoin ETF. While digital assets struggled, US large caps rose 2.0% on the [[markets|Financial Markets]] and the VIX volatility index fell 5.3% in the latest data. This divergence suggests that crypto-specific factors are currently outweighing general risk appetite.

Precious metals provided a sharp contrast. Silver gained 7.8% and copper rose 2.9% on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]]. This pattern, where copper and shares rise together, is consistent with confidence in global growth, though one session is not enough to establish a trend.

Market participants will watch for a stabilization in fund flows to see if selling pressure abates. Continued outflows would strengthen the bearish interpretation, while a quick rebound would suggest a short-lived adjustment.

briefs.markets: US large caps rose 2.0% as the 10-year yield fell 6 basis points in the latest data, suggesting markets are pricing in cooler inflation on the [[markets|Financial Markets]].
briefs.energy: Crude prices were quiet in the latest data, with WTI up 1.0% to $82.24, though the [[energy|Energy Terminal]] shows a 25.0% decline over the last month.
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin fell 2.1% to $59,230 amid confirmed ETF outflows, while the dollar gained slightly against the euro and yen on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] page.
briefs.metals: Silver surged 7.8% and copper gained 2.9% on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]], moves that are consistent with renewed confidence in global industrial growth.
briefs.estate: The [[estate|Estate Index]] shows a sharp divergence in global property, with Moldova rising 33.7% while the Chinese market has contracted by 6.3%.
briefs.corporate: The [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]] identifies APA Corporation as a top performer with an EB Score of 89, despite a generally risk-off quarterly environment.
briefs.outlook: The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] highlights that semiconductors and AI themes have faced steep declines this quarter, falling 25.2% and 21.6% respectively.
briefs.islamic: The EB Shariah US 100 rose 2.0% to 111.77 on the [[islamic|Islamic Investment]] page, tracking the broader market gain with a 9.1% year-to-date return.
